shots.title: Color picker by srinivas.design on Dribbble
shots.note: Material palette grid of named colour tiles, Palette and Hex dropdowns, live Material Design app preview at right.

patterns: The workhorse layout is a 2D saturation/brightness square with a hue strip (vertical beside it, or horizontal under it), then a hex field; a checkerboard alpha strip is added in about half of those.

Preset swatches are the second family: grids (hues across, shades down), tint-to-shade ramps per theme colour, or a short row of dots; several pair them with a 'My colours / + Add' row of saved swatches.

Picking from a photo (pins, crosshair or loupe on an image) that extracts a palette with hex labels and copy buttons is now the third most common family, especially in the Daily UI #060 shots and on phones; a 'copied' state on the tile recurs (57, retry 95).
Mode switching (HEX / RGB / HSL, sometimes CMYK / LAB / HSB) is usually a small dropdown next to the value fields, not a full tab bar.

Builder-grade pickers (Framer 44, Sergey Morozov 7, ram 81) add Solid / Gradient (Linear) tabs, an eyedropper, opacity %, old-vs-new compare and OK / cancel; these are the closest models for our builder.
Colour wheels and hue rings appear mainly in smart-light and phone apps where a thumb drags a large target; desktop editors prefer the square.

Worth copying: theme-colour ramps with a 'My color + Add' row (3, 4); a contrast checker inside the picker with ratio, AA badge and fg/bg swap (68); live preview of the palette on a real page (48, 73); a named token chip ('Button #44cd89') that opens the picker (83).
Rare in this set: no OKLCH / LAB value inputs (LAB appears only as a mode pill in 15), no visible gradient-stops editor, and a WCAG hint in only one shot. These gaps are where we can do better.

Coverage: 117 images opened (100 in the first folder + 17 re-crawled). The 18 captcha pages were dropped; of the 99 real pages, 75 are pickers and 24 are not (listing page, illustrations, unrelated UI).
